info.name: SWE2106 Class Attendance API — Group G
info.description:
# Class Attendance Management System — API Collection

**Course:** SWE2106 Internet Technologies and Web Design · Etivity 5 · **Group G** · Mbarara University of Science and Technology

## How to use this collection

1. Start MySQL (port 3307): `database\start-database.cmd`
2. Start the API: `npm start` (server listens on `http://localhost:3000`)
3. Run the folders **in order from top to bottom** — each request sets variables used by later ones.
4. Before re-running the whole collection, run the **8 · Cleanup** folder first (or reset everything with `npm run seed`).

## Response envelope

Every endpoint answers with the same envelope:

```json
{ "success": true,  "message": "...", "data": { } }
{ "success": false, "error": { "code": "VALIDATION_ERROR", "message": "...", "details": [ "..." ] } }
```

## Error codes

| Code | HTTP | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| VALIDATION_ERROR | 400 | missing/invalid fields, bad formats, unknown status |
| NOT_ENROLLED | 400 | student is not enrolled in the course |
| UNAUTHORIZED | 401 | missing/invalid/expired token |
| INVALID_CREDENTIALS | 401 | wrong email or password |
| FORBIDDEN | 403 | role not allowed (or student viewing another student) |
| *_NOT_FOUND | 404 | referenced record does not exist |
| DUPLICATE_ENTRY | 409 | duplicate course code / enrolment / attendance entry |
| SERVER_ERROR | 500 | unexpected fault |

| admin | collins.murungi@must.ac.ug | admin123 |
| lecturer (SWE2106, SWE2101) | dickens.aine@must.ac.ug | lecturer123 |

## Attendance workflow demonstrated

login → list courses → (admin) create course → enrol student → (lecturer) create session → record attendance one-by-one or save the whole register → view registers → summaries.

item.name: 0 · Health & Logins
item.description: Verifies the API is alive and obtains bearer tokens for each role.

request.description: Confirms the API is running and the MySQL database is reachable.
System administrator login. Saves the token as {{adminToken}}.
Lecturer login. Saves the token as {{lecturerToken}}.
Second lecturer — used later to prove a lecturer cannot manage a course they do not teach.
Student login. Saves the token as {{studentToken}}.
Academic Registrar staff login (read-only role). Saves the token as {{registrarToken}}.
Shows the account attached to the bearer token.

item.name: 1 · Courses
item.description: Course listing and creation. Lecturers see only their courses, students only enrolled courses, staff everything.

request.description: Lecturers receive only the courses they teach, with student/session counts and attendance rate.
An enrolled student can view the course detail. (A student not enrolled would get 403.)
Admin creates a demonstration course. If you re-run the collection without cleanup this returns 409 (code already exists).

exec: pm.test("Course code already exists (409) — run the Cleanup folder first", () => pm.response.to.have.status(409));

request.description: Server-side duplicate check: course codes are unique.
Required fields are checked before anything is saved; the response lists every problem.
Only the system administrator can create courses.

item.name: 2 · Enrolments
item.description: Enrolling students into courses, with duplicate and unknown-student checks.

item.name: List students not enrolled in TEST101

request.description: The ?not_enrolled_in= filter powers the enrolment form in the frontend.

exec: pm.test("At least one student available", () => pm.expect(b.data.length).to.be.above(0));

request.description: Enrols the selected student into the demonstration course.
A student can only be enrolled once per course (unique constraint in the database + server-side check).
Referencing a student that does not exist returns a clear 404.
Enrolled students of SWE2106 (11 seeded students).

exec: pm.test("9 students are enrolled in SWE2106", () => pm.expect(pm.response.json().data.length).to.eql(9));

item.name: 3 · Class Sessions
item.description: Creating and listing class sessions for a course.

request.description: Lists sessions with recorded counts. Finds the empty 'Building REST APIs with Express' session for the attendance demos.

exec: pm.test("8 sessions exist for SWE2106", () => pm.expect(b.data.length).to.eql(8));
const demo = b.data.find(s => s.topic === 'Building REST APIs with Express');
pm.test("Demo session has an empty register", () => pm.expect(demo.recorded_count).to.eql(0));

request.description: Creates a session in the demonstration course.
Dates must be YYYY-MM-DD.
Ibrahim teaches SWE2104, not SWE2106 — only the course lecturer or an admin can create sessions.

item.name: 4 · Attendance
item.description: Recording, updating, validating and bulk-saving attendance for the empty demo session.

request.description: Lecturer records student #5 (Nkamushaba Saviour) as present.
The same student cannot have two entries for one session — this is the core duplicate rule.
Only present, absent and late are valid statuses.

exec: pm.test("Message lists allowed statuses", () => pm.expect(pm.response.json().error.message).to.include('present, absent, late'));

request.description: Student #14 (Namara Jane, a fictional demo student) is not enrolled in SWE2106 — attendance cannot be recorded for her.
Students cannot record attendance.
Updates student #5 from present to late.
The frontend 'Save register' button calls this endpoint. All entries are validated first; if any entry is invalid nothing is saved (transaction).
The same student twice in one request is rejected before anything is saved.
Full register: every enrolled student with their current status (or unrecorded) plus summary counts.
Students only see their own attendance, never the full class register.

item.name: 5 · Histories
item.description: Attendance histories with the students-only-see-their-own rule.

request.description: Savour (id 5) reads her own attendance history.
Savour (id 5) tries to read Jastina's (id 6) history — rejected.
Staff can review any student. The course_id filter narrows the history to SWE2106.
Profile plus the courses the student is enrolled in.

item.name: 6 · Summaries
item.description: Reporting endpoints by course, session, student and platform-wide.

request.description: Per-student statistics for SWE2106: present, absent, late counts and attendance rate.
Counts for the demo session after the attendance entries recorded above.
Per-course attendance breakdown for Savour.
Platform-wide totals and per-course attendance rates.
The platform overview is restricted to administrators and registrar staff.

item.name: 7 · Access Control
item.description: Security edge cases: missing tokens, bad tokens, wrong passwords, unknown routes.

request.description: Every endpoint except /api/auth/login and /api/health requires a bearer token.
Tokens are checked against active sessions.
Failed logins always return the same generic message (no hints about which part was wrong).
Unknown API routes return a JSON 404 in the standard envelope.
User administration is admin-only.

item.name: 8 · Cleanup
item.description: Removes the records created by this collection so it can be run again. Run this folder before re-running the collection (or reset everything with `npm run seed`).

request.description: Deletes the attendance entry recorded earlier for student 5. Also repeat for students 6 and 7 below (or run this request with each id).
Cleanup for student 6.
Cleanup for student 7.
Deleting a course cascades to its enrolments, sessions and attendance entries.
